transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because everybody keeps saying I’m acting crazy, especially my husband, and then people at the warehouse too. But I’m not stupid, I can see what’s going on. They’ve been watching what I do, like tracking my moves, and messing with the pallet counts so I don’t get that supervisor spot. I’ve worked hard there, you know, and it’s like every time I get close, suddenly the numbers don’t match and everyone looks at me funny.
Do you believe that people are specifically targeting you or plotting against you, beyond what others might consider normal workplace issues?

Yes, I do. I mean, people can say it’s just work stuff, but it’s not normal when my husband is acting like I’m crazy and then the warehouse people are watching what I’m doing. Like they know when I move things, and then somehow the pallet counts get changed, and it makes me look bad.

And I’ve been trying to get that supervisor spot, you know? I’ve been there doing the lifting and the counting and all that, and then suddenly it’s like everybody’s looking at me sideways. My aunt used to say when people smile too much at work, they’re hiding something—anyway, yeah, I think they’re doing it on purpose to keep me from moving up.
Have you ever seen, heard, or felt things that others around you don’t seem to notice?

Yeah… sometimes. Like I’ll be in the aisle at work, or even at home folding clothes, and I hear this man’s voice, clear like he’s right there, saying, Nicole, check it again. And I turn, because I think somebody’s behind me, but nobody is near me.

It’s not like the normal warehouse noise either, because I know what that sounds like—the forklifts, the beeping, people yelling about shipments. This is different. Anyway, I’ll check the count again because, you know, if I don’t, then they’ll say I messed it up.
Have you ever believed something strongly that others say isn’t true, even when they give you evidence to the contrary?

Yeah, I mean… that’s kind of what’s happening. My husband keeps saying I’m “making it up” or that I’m acting crazy, and the people at the warehouse act like there’s nothing going on, but I know what I’m seeing.

They watch what I do, like when I move pallets or check counts, and then somehow the numbers change and it falls back on me. And it’s always right when I’m trying to get considered for that supervisor spot. Like, that doesn’t just happen over and over for no reason.

People can show me whatever paper they want, but I’ve worked there long enough to know when something’s being messed with. My cousin had a boss like that once—well, not exactly the same, but people do things when they don’t want you moving up. So yes, I believe they’re doing it.

Can you tell me more about the belief that people are changing the pallet counts to make you look bad? Have you seen direct proof that this is happening, or is it something you know based on how things keep turning out?

I mean, I haven’t caught somebody with a pen in their hand changing it right in front of me, if that’s what you mean. But I know. Because I do the count, I know what I moved, and then later it’s different and everybody acts like I’m the one who can’t keep track.

That’s why I came in, really, because my husband keeps saying I’m acting crazy, and the warehouse people do too in their own way, like they watch my moves and then pretend nothing happened. It’s always around the supervisor thing too, like when I’m trying to show I can handle more. My old manager used to say numbers don’t lie, but people can make numbers say what they want, you know? So no, I don’t have a picture or anything, but I know they’re doing it to make me look bad and keep me from getting that spot.
When you hear the voice saying 'Nicole, check it again,' do you ever doubt that it’s real, or do you always believe it’s actually happening?

I mean… in the moment it feels real. Like clear as day, a man’s voice saying, Nicole, check it again, and I’ll look around because it sounds like somebody is right there.

Sometimes after, when nobody’s near me, I think maybe I missed something or maybe it was from another aisle or the TV at home or whatever, but then it happens when I’m folding clothes too, and there’s nobody there. So… I guess I don’t always know what to think, but when I hear it, it feels like it’s actually happening.
Have you ever believed something was happening that you know other people would say is impossible or makes no sense at all?

I mean… impossible, I don’t know. People say it makes no sense, like my husband says that, and the people at the warehouse act like I’m crazy. But I came in because I know they’ve been watching what I do there.

Like I’ll move pallets, check the counts, try to make sure everything’s right, and then somehow the numbers are different later. And it’s right when I’m trying to get looked at for that supervisor spot. That’s the part people act like I’m just connecting dots that aren’t there, but I’m not stupid. I’ve worked enough jobs to know when people are trying to keep somebody in their place.

My aunt used to say, “Don’t let people smile in your face and mess with your money,” and that’s kind of what it feels like. So maybe other people say it’s impossible or doesn’t make sense, but to me it makes sense because it keeps happening.
Have you ever believed something so strongly that even when people showed you clear proof it wasn’t true, you still knew in your mind that it was? Something that might not make sense to other people?

I guess… yeah, maybe that. My husband says he has “proof,” but his proof is just people at work saying I messed up or the count was entered wrong, like that’s supposed to settle it.

But I know what I did. I know what pallets I moved, I know when I checked them. And then later the numbers are different, and everybody looks at me like I’m losing it. It’s always when I’m trying to get that supervisor spot too, which is not a coincidence.

It’s like when my cousin used to get blamed for stuff at school because the teacher already decided he was trouble — after that, everything he did looked wrong. That’s how it feels at the warehouse. They watch my moves, then they act like nothing happened. So even if people keep telling me I’m wrong, I still know they’re changing those counts to make me look bad.
Have you ever believed something was happening that wasn’t obvious to other people, even if it seemed plausible to you, like someone was trying to undermine you at work without clear evidence?

Yeah… that’s pretty much what I’m talking about. Like, it’s not like they come up and say, “Nicole, we’re doing this to you,” but I can see it.

I came in because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I’m crazy, like I’m making it up, but I know they’ve been watching what I do. I’ll move a pallet, check the count, and then later it’s different, and somehow it lands back on me. And it’s happening right when that supervisor spot is around, so… I mean, that’s not nothing.

My old manager at another place used to do stuff like that too, not the same exact thing, but you know, picking who they want and then making everybody else look bad. People act like jobs are fair, but they’re not. So yeah, even if I don’t have a video or whatever, I know they’re changing those pallet counts to keep me from getting that position.
Have you ever believed something so strongly that it felt completely true to you, even when there was no clear evidence or other people could not understand why you believed it?

Yeah… I mean, that’s why I came in, really. My husband keeps saying I don’t have “real proof,” and the people at the warehouse act like I’m just making noise, but I know they’ve been watching my moves.

Like I’ll do the pallets, check the counts, and then later something’s changed, and somehow it makes me look bad. And it’s all right when that supervisor spot is coming up. That’s not just in my head. People do stuff like that at jobs all the time—my cousin had something like that happen with a manager, not with pallets, but with people setting you up and then smiling like everything’s fine.

So yeah, other people may not understand why I believe it, but I know they’re changing those pallet counts to keep me from getting that position.
Can you think of a time when someone showed you clear proof that something you believed wasn’t true, and even after seeing that proof, you still knew deep down that your belief was right?

Yeah… I mean, my husband tried to show me, like, messages from work or whatever, saying the counts were entered wrong or that someone else checked it. But that’s not really proof to me, because those same people are the ones in on it, you know?

It reminds me of when my aunt had this landlord who would write things down after the fact and then act like it had always been that way. Paper can say anything. People act like if it’s on a screen, it’s the truth, but somebody puts it there.

So yeah, even when they’re showing me that, I still know what I saw. I came in because everybody keeps acting like I’m crazy, but I know they’ve been watching my moves at the warehouse and changing those pallet counts so I don’t get that supervisor spot.
Have you ever believed something so strange or unusual that even other people who were going through similar situations would not find it believable?

I don’t know if I’d call it strange, because to me it makes sense. But other people act like it’s this big impossible thing.

I came in because my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy, like I’m just stirring stuff up, but I know they’ve been watching what I do. Like every move I make with those pallets, and then the counts get changed, and somehow I’m the one looking bad. And it’s right when that supervisor spot is there, so… I mean, maybe somebody else at work would say, “Oh no, they wouldn’t do all that,” but people do a lot when they want someone out of the way.

My husband says I’m taking it too far, but he doesn’t work there, you know? He doesn’t see how they look at me or how things get switched around. So maybe other people don’t believe it, but I know they’re doing it to keep me from getting that position.
Have you ever believed something so unusual or impossible that even you yourself thought it was strange at the time, but still felt it was true?

I mean… I don’t think it’s impossible. That’s the thing. Other people make it sound like it’s some wild story, but to me it lines up.

Like, I came in because my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy, but I know they’ve been watching my moves. The pallet counts don’t just change by themselves. And it’s funny how it all happens when that supervisor spot is coming up.

I guess sometimes I’ve thought, like, “Why would they go through all that trouble?” But then people do petty stuff at jobs all the time. My old neighbor used to say workplaces are worse than family reunions, everybody smiling and then doing something behind your back. So yeah, maybe it sounds strange to other people, but I still feel like it’s true. They’re changing those counts to keep me from getting that position.
Have you ever believed something that you yourself recognized as completely out of the ordinary, like something that could not possibly be true, even by normal real-world standards?

I don’t know about “could not possibly be true.” That sounds like… I don’t know, like movie stuff or something.

What I’m saying isn’t like that to me. I came in because my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy, but I know they’ve been watching my moves. And those pallet counts—those don’t just change for no reason. It’s right when I’m trying for that supervisor spot, too.

I mean, people can say, “Oh, nobody would do that,” but people do things at work all the time. My cousin had a job where they’d mess with her schedule and then act like she forgot, so… it’s not impossible. It’s just nobody wants to admit what’s going on.
Have you ever believed something that you yourself realized was completely implausible or bizarre, even while you were believing it?

I mean… bizarre to me? Not really. I know people keep using words like that, like “implausible,” but if you worked there you’d see what I’m talking about.

I came in because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I’m crazy, but I know they’ve been watching my moves. Like, they know where I’m at, what pallets I’m touching, and then the counts come back different and somehow it points at me. And it’s right when that supervisor spot is up, which is not a coincidence.

I guess I’ve had moments where I’m like, “This is a lot,” you know, like why can’t people just do their job and go home. My aunt used to say some folks smile in your face and count your money behind your back—she was like that about everybody at church too, always saying who was fake. But that doesn’t mean it’s impossible. It just means people don’t want to admit how far they’ll go to block somebody.
